title: Saudi Arabia Forces Postponement of Iran-Gulf Hormuz Talks in Salalah, Oman
detail: The first Gulf-Iran gathering since the war began -- foreign ministers and officials from Iran, Iraq and the Gulf Cooperation Council states meeting in Salalah, Oman to discuss an Omani-brokered temporary Strait of Hormuz shipping arrangement -- was postponed Sunday night after Saudi Arabia submitted last-minute amendments to the Iran-Oman proposal, concerned its wording would lock in an unacceptable status quo. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi wrote that 'in the interests of consensus the regional meeting set for tomorrow in Salalah has been postponed,' with no new date announced. The underlying bilateral Iran-Oman plan envisioned inbound vessels using Iranian territorial waters and outbound vessels routed mostly through Omani waters, with voluntary tolls for navigation, environmental protection and rescue operations. Iran's Foreign Ministry confirmed the Saudi objection was the reason for the delay; a ministry spokesman said Tehran would next 'decide, in consultation with Oman, how to announce or register the agreement.' Bahrain had already declined to attend over the absence of restored diplomatic ties with Iran.

media.caption: The Salalah, Oman meeting on a temporary Strait of Hormuz shipping arrangement was postponed after Saudi objections, Sept 14, 2026

confidenceReason: On-record statement from Oman's Foreign Minister and Iran's Foreign Ministry, corroborated by Al Jazeera, NPR and CNN reporting; the substance of Saudi Arabia's objections was not independently detailed.

title: Houthis Seize Red Sea's Hanish Islands, Claim Large-Scale Missile and Drone Attack on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid Air Base
detail: Yemen's Houthi movement said it seized the strategic islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish in the southern Red Sea, 160km north of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, after hundreds of government-allied forces withdrew -- the latest step in a rapid Houthi advance that already captured the port city of Mocha and Mayun island inside Bab el-Mandeb earlier in September. The group said Saudi jets had struck Houthi-held areas of Yemen 54 times in the preceding 24 hours (part of a claimed 300+ strikes over five days). Hours later, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed a large-scale ballistic missile and drone attack -- the group's second on the base in under 90 minutes, around 22:40 UTC -- on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait, targeting aircraft hangars, radar, runways and ammunition depots and claiming 'direct hits.' Riyadh did not immediately respond to or confirm the claim. The escalation extends the war's Gulf-of-Aden/Red Sea front, tightening Iran-aligned control over a shipping route that has grown more critical as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively blockaded.

media.caption: Houthi forces expand control over the southern Red Sea's Hanish Islands, Sept 14, 2026

confidenceReason: The Hanish islands seizure is corroborated across Euronews, ABC News Australia and Times of Israel citing Houthi statements and open-source tracking; the King Khalid Air Base damage claim rests solely on the Houthi military spokesman with no Saudi confirmation or independent imagery.
